**DOAC** (Direct Oral Anticoagulants) refers to a class of pharmaceutical products used primarily in the treatment of [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] in Denmark. As a modern alternative to older treatments like [[marevan|Marevan]], DOACs are a central focus of the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database ([[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]]) and the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) quality monitoring efforts. The introduction of DOACs is expected to reduce the long-term risk of severe complications, particularly intracranial bleeding, compared to traditional vitamin K antagonists [^src2].

In terms of safety and pharmacovigilance, national registry data consistently tracks the incidence of severe bleeding events among [[praevalente-patienter-med-atrieflimren|Prævalente patienter med atrieflimren]]. For instance, the 2022–2023 reporting period showed that the rate of [[intrakraniel-bloedning|Intrakraniel blødning]] was 0.52% for patients on DOACs compared to 0.46% for those on Marevan [^src1]. The rate of [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]] was 2.33% for DOACs versus 2.44% for Marevan [^src3]. Subsequent annual reports indicate that intracranial bleeding rates for DOACs were 0.53% in 2024 [^src9] and 0.57% in 2025 [^src16], while severe bleeding rates were 2.30% in 2024 [^src10] and 2.40% in 2025 [^src17]. When analyzing ischemic stroke ([[iskaemisk-apopleksi|Iskæmisk apopleksi]]), the incidence was 0.89% for DOACs and 0.51% for Marevan in the 2024 report [^src8], and 0.86% versus 0.88% respectively in the 2025 report [^src15]. 

Because DOACs are cleared renally, clinical guidelines mandate regular monitoring of kidney function. [[indikator-4b|Indikator 4b]] specifically measures the proportion of prevalent atrial fibrillation patients on DOACs who receive at least one annual measurement of [[s-creatinin|S-creatinin]] or P-creatinin [[npu04998-p-kreatinin|NPU04998 (P-Kreatinin)]] [^src5], [^src6], [^src14]. The national quality standard for this indicator is set at ≥ 95% [^src5]. In the 2024 reporting period, 93.9% of the prevalent population on DOAC therapy met this monitoring requirement nationally [^src7]. 

Pharmacologically, DOACs encompass several specific drug classes and active ingredients tracked in the registry, including dabigatran ([[b01ae07|B01AE07]]), rivaroxaban ([[b01af01|B01AF01]]), apixaban ([[b01af02|B01AF02]]), and edoxaban ([[b01af03|B01AF03]]) [^src22]. Patients receiving combination therapy with both DOAC and Marevan exhibit notably higher risks for adverse outcomes, such as a 4.06% incidence of ischemic stroke [^src18] and a 4.68% incidence of severe bleeding [^src1], highlighting the clinical importance of monotherapy and precise [[antikoagulationsbehandling|antikoagulationsbehandling]] management.

  Type: prognostic

  Type: clinical
- Indikator 4b har standarden ≥ 95 % for andelen af prævalente patienter med atrieflimren i Direkte Orale antikoagulantia (DOAC) med mindst 1 måling af S-creatinin årligt [^src1] (atrieflimren, doac, s-creatinin, indikator-4b)

- På landsplan fik 93,9% den prævalente population af patienter med atrieflimren, som var i DOAC-behandling, målt p-creatinin mindst én gang årligt [^src1] (indikator-4b, atrieflimren, doac)
